artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a nonnegative integer n, define
$$P_n \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{n}{k}^{2}\binom{2k}{k}.$$
Let $p$ be an odd prime. For an integer $a$ not divisible by $p$, let $a^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $a$ modulo $p^2$, and interpret rational expressions of the form $r/s$ (with $\gcd(s,p)=1$) modulo $p^2$ as $r\cdot s^{-1} \pmod{p^2}$.

Decide whether the following two congruences hold.

(i) Suppose $p\equiv 3\pmod 8$ and write $p = x^2 + 2y^2$ with $x,y\in\mathbb Z$ chosen so that $y\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{P_k}{32^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2} \;\equiv\; (-1)^{(y-1)/2}\!\left(2y - \frac{p}{4y}\right)\pmod{p^2}.$$

(ii) Suppose $p\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$ and write $p = x^2 + 2y^2$ with $x\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$, and additionally $y\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$ when $p\equiv 3\pmod 8$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\,P_k}{32^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2} \;\equiv\; \begin{cases} (-1)^{(p-1)/8}\!\left(\dfrac{p}{4x} - \dfrac{x}{2}\right) \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } p\equiv 1\pmod 8,\\[4pt] (-1)^{(y+1)/2}\, y \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } p\equiv 3\pmod 8. \end{cases}$$

Are both conjectured congruences true for every such prime $p$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published proof or disproof of this specific supercongruence (Conjecture A58 in Sun's list of open conjectures on congruences). It belongs to a family of conjectural supercongruences modulo $p^2$ involving the Catalan–Larcombe–French-type numbers $P_n$ and representations $p = x^2+2y^2$, many of which remain open. No definitive resolution was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Surveys progress on Sun-type supercongruences; many conjectures involving sums of P_n type sequences remain open.
